label: late original positions / <DEL> in sequences that begin with s, b, a, k, l, d
explanation: Fires only in the original phase at t>=4 and on the <DEL> step (about 81% / 19% of mass). It never fires during copy or at t<=2. Inside that window the rate goes up with position (orig_idx 8 about 10%) and with L (L=9 holds 48% of mass). The timing alone (phase<=1, t>=5) covers 97% of mass but has only 5% precision. Whether it fires mostly depends on which tokens opened the sequence: first_tok in {s,b,a,k,l,d} gives 2.3-4.4x lift, and requiring orig(1) or orig(2) to be in the same set too raises precision to about 0.3-0.6 but costs recall. That looks like a graded, distributed sum over the early tokens rather than a clean rule. Magnitude is largest on in_tok c (5.5x rate), then digits 1/2 and <DEL>, and on the first occurrence of a token (in_first). It is weak on repeated tokens. Best dev F1 is 0.34 (mass recall 0.50).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=s (+3.85), orig0=b (+3.59), phase=0 & in_tok=c (+3.43), orig1=d (+3.32), orig1=a (+3.26), orig1=s (+3.21). Lower it: phase=2 (-8.05), prev3_tok=- (-7.81), t=3 (-6.91), in_tok=s (-4.78).
